task: match the held planet gear height to the carrier side opening
arm_assignment_evidence: Gear pickup and release coincide with left gripper changes in the reviewed states. Wrist port2 shows the gear gripper; wrist port3 shows the carrier gripper. The recording calibration still marks camera-to-arm assignments unverified.
target_definition: (left tool base Z - right tool base Z) at observation minus the same quantity at the reviewed reference. Positive values mean the gear tool is higher relative to the reference; the corresponding left-only correction is the negative of this value.
target_provenance: Weak kinematic reference from a grasp-preserving demonstration interval. The reference is a visible near-contact pose before release, not measured gear seating or object-center height ground truth.
limitations: No measured camera intrinsics, extrinsics, depth, object poses, or contact event labels are available in these recordings.

Tool Z is reported in each arm's base frame. The label assumes both base Z axes share the vertical direction. Fixed base height offsets cancel within an episode; changing tool rotations and object grasp offsets do not.
The intended opening is the side gap between carrier plates. The carrier center bearing and the top pin bore are different targets.
The held-out episode is reserved before dense extraction. Five episodes provide a small development set, not a hardware success estimate.

episodes.visual_evidence: Gear remains between the jaws while approaching the carrier rim; gear gripper withdraws toward the pin after this interval.
Gear approaches the same peripheral side opening; the selected reference precedes the later release and withdrawal.
Held gear converges on the carrier rim; release and local retry motions later in the recording are excluded.
Gear is transported to the rim and remains grasped during local alignment; later opening and pin transport are excluded.
Held gear approaches the rim; the reference precedes the opening and withdrawal visible around 8–9 seconds.
